title: Cluster occupancy histogram export — 72h sample
body:
Cluster occupancy histogram export — 72h sample (2026-02-11 to 2026-02-13)

Purpose:
This is a lightweight export from the dashboard to capture short-term occupancy and bucketed utilization for capacity planning. Goal: identify persistent under- or over-occupied clusters/pools and short latency bursts that correlate with occupancy spikes. Use for quick policy recommendations for autoscaler knobs and preemption budgets.

Sampling methodology:
- Window: 2026-02-11 00:00 UTC through 2026-02-13 23:59 UTC (72h).
- Metric: per-GPU instantaneous allocation percentage sampled at 1m resolution, aggregated by cluster and pool.
- Occupancy buckets computed per-sample then averaged over the window: 0% (idle), 1-25%, 26-50%, 51-75%, 76-100%.
- Pools: realtime, batch, preemptible.
- Exclusions: diagnostic/test clusters (cluster-dev-*), maintenance windows filtered out (tagged maintenance).

Quick observations / anomalies:
- High idle on batch and preemptible pools (chi-1 batch idle 42.8%, preemptible 51.6%): suggests right-sizing opportunity or moving long-tail batch jobs to a single smaller burst pool.
- SJC realtime cluster shows wider spread and notable 15%+ idle time: uneven request distribution — check routing weight configuration for regional routing lane.
- Preemptible interruption counts spiked on 2026-02-13 across SJC (44 interrupts): likely correlated with scheduled maintenance on underlying host classes (see INFRA-2389).
- p90 util for realtime clusters still high in AMS and CHI (>=90%): these clusters experience short high-load bursts that drive latency; consider adding short-burst headroom or increasing burst-capacity pool size.

Recommendations (short-term, <= 2 weeks):
- Reduce reserve for batch pool in cluster-chi-1 by 12% (move N=8 GPUs to a transient pool): ticket INFRA-2345.
- Create a "burst-realtime" pool in AMS (12 GPUs) with lower preemption budget to absorb p90 spikes: experiment for 7 days, monitor p90 -> target reduction of 10–15% latency tail.
- For SJC realtime, review routing weights on the smart-router: suspected mis-weighting to legacy zone-sjc-east. Owner: Samir.
- Investigate the source of high preemptible interrupts on 2026-02-13; correlate host maintenance logs (INFRA-2389) and consider shifting critical scheduled batch runs out of that window.

Longer-term considerations (quarterly):
- Re-run 14-day occupancy rolling analysis with model-anchored traffic (post-new-model launch) to validate whether higher p90s are steady-state or a burst artifact.
- Add per-job occupancy tagging to capture short-lived model warmup spikes (ticket: TBD).

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Samir: collect router config snapshot for SJC and AMS (slack: #infra-routing).
- [ ] Diego: run a dry-run capacity move of 8 GPUs from chi-1 batch to chi-1 transient pool and measure job queuing over 48h.
- [ ] Maya: schedule follow-up with product to understand upcoming model release traffic patterns (due 2026-02-22).

- Related tickets: INFRA-2345 (batch-rightsize proposal), INFRA-2389 (host maintenance report), INFRA-2410 (routing weight review).
- Quick trace: slack thread #infra-incidents on 2026-02-13 about preempt interruptions.

Data attachment: raw CSV exported from dashboard is attached in the Drive folder (export name: occupancy-72h-2026-02-11-13.csv).

Generated by: Maya Fernandez (manual dashboard export + quick analysis).
Notes: this is intended as an operational snapshot for the on-call and capacity planning sync; not a full reconciled capacity forecast.
